answer.text:
You asked
Where is to_pascal used, and what breaks if I change it?

In short: to_pascal() converts snake_case strings to PascalCase and is used by to_camel(), model creation, and deprecated decorator code to generate field aliases automatically.

Where it lives: pydantic/alias_generators.py:L12

Who depends on it: 16 places depend on it across 8 files. The 5 most important are:

-
`to_camel()` (pydantic/alias_generators.py) — builds on top of to_pascal(), so changes cascade
-
`.create_model()` (pydantic/deprecated/decorator.py) — uses it to auto-generate aliases in dynamically created models
-
`test_snake2pascal()` (tests/test_utils.py) — directly tests the function's core behavior
-
Alias docs (docs/concepts/alias.md) — documents this as a public alias generator feature
-
Deprecated decorator (pydantic/deprecated/decorator.py) — legacy code path relying on it

If you change it: These will likely break:

-
Any model using alias_generator=to_pascal will generate different field names in JSON/dict output
-
The @validate_arguments decorator (now deprecated) won't convert function arguments correctly
-
Tests in tests/test_utils.py will fail immediately (at least test_snake2pascal, test_on_lower_camel_*, test_to_camel_from_camel)
-
User code depending on the documented alias generator behavior

Run these first: pytest tests/test_utils.py tests/test_computed_fields.py tests/test_deprecated.py -xvs

Try this: Open tests/test_utils.py and find test_snake2pascal() to see exactly what transformation is expected, then run that one test to confirm your understanding.
